# dsh-billing-mini-tag
English | 中文

Show the **current session's spend** (`¥x.xx`) at the right end of the composer
statistics row — to

the right of the context-usage meter. Amounts are priced
from the official DeepSeek token quote.
the ¥1.47 on the right is this plugin
## Install
Two routes; use whichever matches how you run DSH.
### 1. Install on the shell

Choose **one** of the four installation methods below. They are alternatives,
not steps to run in se

quence — do not run all four. All four finish with the
same `dsh plugin --profile web add` command;
only the package source differs.
**Method A — npm package (recommended; follows the latest release):**

**Method B — pinned release tarball (reproducible version):**

**Method C — repository main branch (latest development code):**

**Method D — local clone (for development):**
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`dsh plugin add` forwards to pnpm inside the profile directory, so pass an
absolute path — `"$PWD"`

after `cd` does that. A relative `.` would resolve to
the profile directory, not this clone. Update
the clone later with `git pull`.

After choosing one and installing, restart `dsh web`, refresh the page, then
send a message. Run the

same `add` command again, with the same source, to
update; remove with:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The package ships plain JavaScript with no `prepare` script, so a GitHub
install needs neither a bui
ld step nor pnpm's build-script authorization.
### 2. Install on DeepSeek Harness Desktop

1. Open **Plugins** in the sidebar.
2. Choose **Add plugin** → **Install a third-party plugin**.
3.

Paste `dsh-billing-mini-tag` — or `github:Refone/dsh-billing-mini-tag` — into
**Package name or addr

ess**, then press **Install**.
4. Press **Enable now** when DSH offers it, and restart the app if it

asks for a
restart: the host half mounts the cost route, so the first load needs one.
5. Send a mes

sage — `¥` appears at the far right of the composer statistics row,
to the right of the context-usag

¥` appears at the far right of the composer statistics row,
to the right of the context-usage meter.

If npm or GitHub is unreachable, expand **Install source** in the same dialog
and pick a mirror, or

paste the tarball URL from the
releases page.
## What it shows

- **Session spend only.** The tag totals the token usage recorded in the
current session's durable l

og. It is not an account balance and not a
cross-session total.
- **Live while you work.** The brows

er half polls the host route once a second,
so the number moves as steps complete without a page rel

oad.
- **At the right end of the row.** The tag is a `conversation.composer.dock`
entry with `order:

2`. That slot renders before the shipped context-usage
meter, so the pill also carries a positive C

SS `order` to stay to the meter's
right — the original layout — without starting a second line.
## How it works
The package ships two halves:
| Half | Entry | Responsibility |
| Host | `src/index.js` (`.` export) | Serves `GET /plugin-billing-mini-tag/cost?session=<id>`, fold

s the session log per assistant step, and refreshes the official quote. |
| Browser | `src/client.js
` (`./client` export) | Registers the `billing-mini-tag` composer-dock entry and keeps the `¥…` pill
at the right end of the statistics row, right of the context-usage meter. |

The plugin declares no `meta.title`. DSH falls back to the package name
(`dsh-billing-mini-tag`), wh

ich is also the component row's id and module name,
so the component row no longer prints the name t

wice more under its own title.
`locale/*.json` keeps the description — which DSH does not derive fro

m the
package — plus the pill tooltip copy.
The host half:

1. Fetches the official Chinese pricing page at startup and again on every
message send, caching the

last good quote. The request has an 8s timeout and
a built-in quote is used until the first success

ful fetch (and when the page
is unreachable).
2. Folds `assistant/attempt` / `assistant/message` usa

ge events per
`turn:step`; a repeated step replaces its predecessor, and an
`llm/retry-started` make

s the retried attempt bill as a separate call. This
mirrors DSH's own `tokenUsage` projection.
3. Re

members which model actually served each step, so a mid-session model
switch is priced at the right

rate.
4. Returns a rounded display string (`¥0.00`) plus raw tokens, per-model
breakdown, quote sour

ce, and unknown-model names for debugging. Unknown
sessions, unloaded logs, and failed quote fetches

degrade to zero or the
previous quote instead of throwing.

The route is same-origin only: it rejects cross-site callers and accepts
header-less probes only fro

m loopback. A companion debug route,
`GET /plugin-billing-mini-tag/quote`, returns the cached quote

and current
prices. Nothing is sent anywhere except the pricing-page request itself; there
is no tel

rent
prices. Nothing is sent anywhere except the pricing-page request itself; there
is no telemetry.
## Pricing
Prices are CNY per 1M tokens from the official page:
| Bucket | How it is charged |

| Cache hit (input read from cache) | cache-hit price |
| Cache miss (uncached input) | cache-miss p

rice |
| Cache write | cache-miss price |
| Output | output price |

Peak windows are evaluated in Beijing time (no DST): **Mon–Fri 09:00–12:00 and
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements

- DSH **0.2.x** — the package declares `engines.dsh` as `>=0.2.0`, the range
with the composer-dock

list slot this control registers into.
- Node.js **20 or newer**.
- React 18 is provided by the host

(declared as a peer dependency); the plugin
has no runtime dependencies of its own.
- Network acces

s to `api-docs.deepseek.com` for live quotes. Offline installs
still work with the embedded quote.
-

The browser half injects DSH's client `locale` service (shipped with the web
and desktop apps) for

its pill tooltip. The fiber waits for it, so the
tooltip never renders as a raw key.

> **Needs the `webServer` service.** The plugin serves its cost route through
> the shipped `web` bu

ndle, so any profile that mounts it works — the `web`
> profile and the Desktop app's `desktop` prof

ile both do. Installing it into a
> custom profile that only has `dsh-base` leaves the entry waiting

for
> `webServer`, and DSH refuses to boot. Initialize custom profiles from the web
> template (`ds
h --profile <name> --from-default-profile web`).
